solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Element of slapstick comedy is captured differently

indicators.note: arranged differently means the same letters are put in another order

parts.note: the two words supply ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A film buff observes that some piece of slapstick has been filmed in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie in the face is the classic custard-pie gag, a staple prop of knockabout clowning.

clue.text: Feeling concern about knave stealing vehicles

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: showing concern for others
the knave is the jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone worries about a rogue who keeps taking cars.
explanation.walkthrough: In cards the knave and the jack are the same card, so knave stands for the jack.
explanation.definitionFit: Carjacking is the crime of seizing a car, typically from its driver by force.

clue.text: Son accompanying old man in health resort

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
old man is slang for father, hence pa

explanation.surface: A son takes his elderly father to a wellness retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a resort built around mineral springs, visited for health treatments.

clue.text: Give weapons to group, or a bit of kit for the captain

definitions.text: a bit of kit for the captain

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
a band is a group of people

explanation.surface: Either equip a gang with guns, or hand the skipper a piece of gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A team captain in sports such as football or cricket wears an armband to mark the role.

clue.text: Daughter gets rotten roll, a bit of bread abroad

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: something rotten has gone bad and lost its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of roll plus the article a

explanation.surface: A girl is handed a stale bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface keeps us in the bakery, but bread is slang for money; abroad points to a foreign currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and a dollar is a unit of currency used in America and other countries.

clue.text: Tips Lamarck oddly ignored, or Newton?

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones, every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A scientist wonders whether to drop Lamarck's advice and follow Newton instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamarck was a French naturalist, so the surface sets one scientist against another.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac Newton is the physicist, so the question mark marks his first name as an example of the answer.

clue.text: Maintained tidiness needs sorting out

indicators.note: sorting out a muddle means putting things into a fresh order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone claims that neatness is something that needs attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Maintained here is the verb meaning asserted, not kept in repair.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert it firmly, which is what insisted means.

clue.text: Only half of Spanish football team in field

indicators.note: keeping only half a name means the remaining part is thrown away

parts.note: Real Madrid is the famous club from Spain's capital

explanation.surface: Only half of a Spanish football side has taken the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The team's full name has ten letters; the first five remain. Field looks like a football pitch but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A field in the sense of a sphere of activity or knowledge is a realm.

clue.text: Discovered tragic king not losing heart

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: We found out that a doomed monarch kept his courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter O comes out of NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Learnt means found out or came to know, a synonym for discovered.

clue.text: Tiny characters run around US shopping centre

indicators.note: around means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to sprint is to run fast
mall is the American term for a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Little people dash about an American shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters suggests people, but here it means printed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Small print is the tiny lettering of a contract's terms, so its characters are tiny.

clue.text: Back from pyjama party in state of agitation

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, which is what is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone returns from a sleepover all in a fluster.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bustle, a flurry of agitated activity.

clue.text: Defeated in part of cricket match, caught by a crossword setter

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A batsman beaten during an over, out caught by the compiler himself.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a block of six deliveries in cricket; c marks a catch on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcame means beat or got the better of, a synonym for defeated.

clue.text: Bit of Roman arch is made to show radical concept

indicators.note: a bit of a phrase is a run of its letters lifted out whole

parts.note: the run starts at the end of the first word and ends at the start of the last

explanation.surface: A fragment of Roman masonry is built to illustrate a revolutionary notion.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the political idea that the state should be abolished, a radical doctrine.

clue.text: What sounds like requirements for massages

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to match the pronunciation, not the spelling

parts.note: requirements are needs

explanation.surface: A list of what is wanted for a back rub.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work muscle or dough with the hands, so massages is a verb sense matching the answer.

clue.text: After strong wine, a Liberal makes grand entrance

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the first one

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A tipsy Liberal politician sweeps into the room in style.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is an imposing doorway or gate, a grand way in.

clue.text: Supervise poetry in Old English

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: An instruction to oversee some poems written in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface, in Old English describes the poems' language; cryptically it says where the poetry sits.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct work, a synonym for supervise.

clue.text: Where to see pictures contained by graphic in email

indicators.note: contained by says the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the run starts at the end of the first word and runs into the last

explanation.surface: Images sent within a graphic attached to an email.
explanation.walkthrough: Pictures here means films, the old word for movies.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema is a theatre where films, or moving pictures, are shown.

clue.text: Fruit from can — entire bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fruit taken from a tin that is entirely bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Spy perhaps not a lady?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a secret ... is one example
second meaning, split in two: a gent, the opposite of a lady

explanation.surface: Suspicion that an undercover operative is not as ladylike as she seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into A GENT; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is an operative such as a spy, an example of the word's meaning.

clue.text: 501 pence for guacamole, say

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and I is 1
P is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: A price tag of 501p for a tub of avocado dip.
explanation.definitionFit: Guacamole is an example of a dip, a sauce for scooping with crisps or bread.

clue.text: French physicist's mother backing his father?

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word reads right to left

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a French father is a père

explanation.surface: A scientist's mother supports his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: His father is French, as the physicist is, so the French word père is used.
explanation.definitionFit: André-Marie Ampère was the French physicist who gave his name to the unit of current.

clue.text: American reversing boat reduced fare from Japan

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: US is short for American

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a ship is a boat

explanation.surface: An American backs a shortened boat out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, and fare means food.

clue.text: Leaders of some key industries go downhill rapidly

indicators.note: leaders are the ones out in front, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Bosses of major businesses are declining fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Go downhill sounds like economic decline, but it is a literal descent on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To ski is to glide down snowy slopes, travelling downhill quickly.

clue.text: Artist gets drunk, one making clever plans

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A painter becomes intoxicated and starts scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist is a person who devises long-term plans, especially shrewd ones.
